pr_body:
Fixes #62542

Previously, the --global flag to demo had some inconsistent behavior:
some of the time, the actual "global" latencies were double what we
would expect. The reason for this was that we were accidentally only
introducing a delay on one of the sides of the connection, some of the
time.

The fix was to change a method to use a pointer receiver :)

Release note (cli change): fix the artificial latencies introduced by
the --global flag to demo.

issue_context.title: demo: global simulated latency does not work with bi-directional streams
issue_context.body:
I haven't gotten to the root cause of this, but something is wrong with the simulated latency of Raft in `demo --global`. As we can see below, the 130ms for a write is about double what we expect.

```
> ./cockroach demo --nodes=9 --global --empty

demo@127.0.0.1:26257/defaultdb> create table kv (k int primary key, v int);
CREATE TABLE

Time: 5ms total (execution 5ms / network 0ms)

demo@127.0.0.1:26257/defaultdb> show ranges from table kv;
  start_key | end_key | range_id | range_size_mb | lease_holder | lease_holder_locality | replicas |                             replica_localities
------------+---------+----------+---------------+--------------+-----------------------+----------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NULL      | NULL    |       37 |             0 |            1 | region=us-east1,az=b  | {1,3,8}  | {"region=us-east1,az=b","region=us-west1,az=a","region=europe-west1,az=d"}
(1 row)

Time: 337ms total (execution 337ms / network 0ms)

demo@127.0.0.1:26257/defaultdb> insert into kv values (1, 2);
INSERT 1

Time: 130ms total (execution 130ms / network 0ms)
```

We see from traces that this time is all spent in Raft. My current guess is that Raft's approach to establish a separate gRPC stream in each direction and send requests and responses on the "sender" side of each stream is tripping up the `delayingConn`. Maybe it expects requests and responses to be matched up more closely, as they are in a unary RPC. Or maybe the streams are causing issues because artificial delays aren't being pipelined properly across multiple requests in the same direction. I'm not sure, but something is going wrong here.

I suspect this is also contributing to the issues we've seen with DistSQL flow setup in https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/CJGSARZJR/p1616188441010400.

cc. @ajstorm. Given our desire to use `demo --global` more, do you view this as a GA-blocker?
comments:
My feeling is that strictly speaking this isn't a GA blocker.  Even though
we're hoping to use --global to showcase multi-region, if the latencies are
higher than they should be, that wouldn't prevent its use.

I know it's early in the investigation, but do you have a sense for the
likelihood that what we find will be backportable?

I imagine whatever we find would be backportable, because this code is only used for `demo --global` and a fix is likely isolated. But as you say, it's early in the investigation.

The patch in #62679 I think will fix this issue. The problem was that we were only introducing the delay on one side some of the time. So some of the time, like in the network latencies chart in the DB Console, the latencies looked correct. But other times, the delay was introduced on both sides and we got double the expected latencies.

However, I am noticing that on the very first time we run an insert, we do get higher latencies than expected. I think this is because connection establishment takes extra roundtrips, but I have no idea? Have a look at this log, from a binary built after the linked PR:

```

------------+---------+----------+---------------+--------------+-----------------------+----------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NULL      | NULL    |       37 |      0.000024 |            1 | region=us-east1,az=b  | {1,8,9}  | {"region=us-east1,az=b","region=us-west1,az=c","region=europe-west1,az=d"}
(1 row)
```

Nice! Thanks for tracking this down.

> However, I am noticing that on the very first time we run an insert, we do get higher latencies than expected. I think this is because connection establishment takes extra roundtrips, but I have no idea?

This could be due to table descriptor leasing? Or maybe priming the dist sender cache? A trace of the INSERT should be pretty telling.
Ugh, that paste got really messed up. Anyway, I think the top part has what we're looking for.

I think we see the time spent in Raft, but it's a little tough to tell because most of the tracing spans at that level are async so they didn't end up here. If you traced this using Jaeger, it may be more informative. We could be waiting for the leader election or lease to be acquired on this new range.
